sources.title: Open-Meteo Weather API
sources.applicability: Hourly/daily temperature, precipitation, and relative humidity forecast
sources.cautions: Modeled regional weather; does not measure microclimate in an individual container.

red.title: Likely Ready for Harvest
red.summary: Fruit displays characteristic mature-red coloration. Check firmness manually before picking.
caveats: Color alone can be misleading for non-red cultivars (e.g., green-when-ripe, yellow, or purple varieties).
Gently squeeze to confirm slight give and fruit ease of detachment at the calyx.
red.next_action: Gently check firmness. If eating fresh today, harvest when fully colored. If storing or transporting, slight firmness is preferred.

turning.title: Approaching Harvest (Breaker/Turning Stage)
turning.summary: Fruit shows initial pink/orange blush indicating the onset of ripening.
caveats: Ripening progression depends on temperature (optimal between 20°C and 25°C; stalls above 30°C or below 10°C).
Can be harvested at breaker stage to avoid field pests/cracking and finished indoors at room temperature.
turning.next_action: Inspect daily or harvest at breaker stage to finish ripening indoors out of direct sun.

green.title: Not Yet Ready / Immature Stage
green.summary: Fruit appears green without color break.
caveats: Mature-green tomatoes have reached full size, white locular jelly, and can ripen off-vine if frost threatens.
Immature green fruit will not ripen satisfactorily off-vine.
green.next_action: Allow fruit to remain on vine unless frost is imminent. Monitor for breaker blush.

uncertain.title: Visual Analysis Uncertain / Retake Photo
uncertain.summary: Visual stage could not be reliably determined due to angle, glare, occlusion, or lack of visual reference.
caveats: Camera angle, lighting, distance, and foliage occlusion prevent reliable color assessment.
uncertain.next_action: Take a close-up photo in indirect natural light showing the whole fruit and calyx.

dry_at_5cm.title: Check Soil & Likely Water
dry_at_5cm.summary: Physical root-zone soil check indicates dryness 5 cm below surface.
dry_at_5cm.rationale: Direct soil moisture assessment confirms root-zone depletion regardless of ambient air humidity.
caveats: Air relative humidity does not reflect root-zone soil water.
Ensure containers or beds have proper drainage to avoid waterlogging.
dry_at_5cm.next_action: Apply water at the soil base (avoid wetting leaves) until water moistens the root zone evenly.

moist.title: Soil Moisture Adequate — Monitor
moist.summary: Root-zone check indicates moist soil; water demand is satisfied.
moist.rationale: Sufficient root-zone moisture prevents stress and reduces blossom end rot risk.
caveats: Avoid unnecessary watering which can leach nutrients and increase root rot risk.
moist.next_action: Recheck in 24–48 hours, especially during high temperature periods.

wet.title: Soil Saturated — Avoid Watering
wet.summary: Soil is saturated or waterlogged; additional irrigation is contraindicated.
wet.rationale: Excessive moisture depletes soil oxygen and promotes fungal pathogens and root hypoxia.
caveats: Persistent waterlogging causes leaf chlorosis and wilting resembling drought stress.
wet.next_action: Allow soil to drain and aerate. Check pot drainage holes or bed drainage channels.

unknown.title: Check Soil Physically Before Deciding
unknown.summary: No direct soil moisture data available.
unknown.rationale: Neither ambient humidity, temperature, nor ultrasonic distance measures soil moisture.
caveats: Air humidity is NOT soil moisture. Do not guess irrigation needs without a tactile soil check or probe.
unknown.next_action: Insert finger or trowel 5–10 cm into the soil near the root zone to determine moisture.

no_symptoms.title: Insufficient Evidence for Fertilization
no_symptoms.summary: No nutrient stress detected and no laboratory soil test provided.
no_symptoms.rationale: Visual inspection and ambient sensors cannot determine nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium levels.
caveats: Routine fertilizer application without soil testing can cause salt buildup or excessive vegetative growth at the expense of fruit.
no_symptoms.next_action: Maintain regular balanced organic mulch or follow scheduled compost regimen; conduct annual extension soil test.

yellowing.title: Visible Chlorosis (Yellowing) — Investigation Needed
yellowing.summary: Foliage shows yellowing patterns, but specific cause cannot be verified without soil/root inspection.
yellowing.rationale: Yellowing can stem from nitrogen deficiency, natural lower-leaf senescence, overwatering, root rot, spider mites, or soil pH imbalance.
caveats: Do NOT immediately apply nitrogen. If caused by overwatering or root disease, added fertilizer worsens damage.
yellowing.next_action: Examine leaf location (lower vs new growth), inspect soil moisture for waterlogging, and submit a soil sample to local extension.

browning_spots.title: Foliar Spots / Necrosis — Investigate Pathogens or Osmotic Stress
browning_spots.summary: Foliage displays necrotic margins or spots; potential early blight, septoria, or salt burn.
browning_spots.rationale: Leaf spotting is predominantly fungal or bacterial rather than simple nutrient starvation.
caveats: Fertilizing will not cure fungal leaf spots and excess fertilizer may accelerate foliage vulnerability.
browning_spots.next_action: Prune affected lower leaves, avoid overhead splashing, improve airflow, and consult local extension pathology diagnostics.

wilting.title: Visible Wilting — Check Soil Moisture & Vascular Health
wilting.summary: Plant displays loss of turgor pressure; could be drought, root rot, or vascular wilt.
wilting.rationale: Wilting occurs when root water uptake fails to match transpiration, either from dry soil or damaged root systems in saturated soil.
caveats: Do NOT fertilize a wilting plant.
wilting.next_action: Perform immediate 5 cm soil moisture probe. If wet, suspect root rot; if dry, water deeply at base.
